evidence.quote: Nvidia’s backstop program is typically six years in length, and during these six years, Nvidia stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over the time period. Each Neocloud is expected to negotiate the backstop terms individually, and we can expect that different Neoclouds may end up with different revenue share and backstop schedules. The below table is an illustrative example to explain the basic terms of the program – we present a backstop pricing curve that we believe to be on the lower end of the backstop range – in this case at an average of $2.36 over the six-year period, but we expect that most Neoclouds will negotiate higher backstops.

evidence.quote: We see that the short-term 1y rental book scenario clearly offers the best IRR among the backstopped scenarios at 25.4%, and these IRRs could realize even higher if the rental market turns out to be strong enough such that 1y and shorter rental rates decay by less than we modeled in the curve below. As expected, the IRRs are higher without a backstop – reaching as high as 40.7% when renting for 1y tenors with no backstop.
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis models a 25.4% IRR for a neocloud’s one-year rental book under Nvidia’s backstop, rising to as much as 40.7% without a backstop; it says returns could be higher if short-term rental rates decline less than modeled.
evidence.speaker: newsletter.semianalysis.com (analyst)

evidence.quote: When it comes to the Nvidia backstop, banks look at the DSCR ratios assuming revenue earned under the scenario where the backstop is activated. evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: In 2025, we wrote extensively about how datacenter capacity was the bottleneck for AI compute growth. By early 2026, the datacenter supply situation improved considerably, but it became clear that chip production was now the limiting constraint. Now – mid-way through the year – it is clear that financing will now be one of the most significant obstacles to ramping large scale compute broadly available to everyone.
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis judged that financing had become one of the biggest obstacles to broadly scaling AI compute by mid-2026, after datacenter supply improved and chip production became the prior constraint.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: Neoclouds have also had a strong incentive to stick with this recipe. To fund a cluster that they intend to rent on shorter terms with a broad book of customers, a Neocloud would have to fall back on unsecured funding. For a top Neocloud, this would mean paying an additional 4% interest, which would significantly impact the economics of the deal given the 70-80% loan to value ratios used to finance GPUs. In our modelling, we show that increasing funding from an all-in cost of 5.62% to an all-in cost of 10% drops PBT margins from 14.8% down to only 5.4%.
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis modeled a top Neocloud's PBT margin falling from 14.8% to 5.4% if its funding cost rose from 5.62% to 10%; it said unsecured borrowing could cost about 4 percentage points more and GPU financing typically uses 70–80% LTV.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: We think that initial lending will be at a wider spread than the current 5y backstopped hyperscale deals which come in at around SOFR + 225bps (roughly equivalent to a Z-spread of 195bps, or about 5.9% total yield) but at a tighter spread than CoreWeave’s 5-year unsecured corporate bond which has a yield of ~10% (roughly equivalent to Z-spread of 600bps).
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis expected initial lending for Nvidia-backstopped GPU clusters to price wider than five-year hyperscale-backed loans at about 5.9% yield, but tighter than CoreWeave's five-year unsecured bonds at about 10%.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: This is why Nvidia has stepped in and has started backstopping GPU rental offtakes themselves . In the backstop program, Nvidia provides a take-or-pay commitment to Neoclouds – a minimum revenue guarantee on the underlying GPU capacity. In exchange for this backstop, Nvidia also shares in a portion of the Neocloud’s revenue earned above the backstop level.
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis reported that Nvidia had started providing Neoclouds take-or-pay minimum-revenue guarantees on GPU capacity in return for a share of revenue above the backstop level.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: Here, Nvidia is diving even deeper, as it has started backstopping datacenter leases.
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis reported that Nvidia had also started backstopping datacenter leases.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: Nvidia’s backstop program is typically six years in length, and during these six years, Nvidia stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over the time period. Each Neocloud is expected to negotiate the backstop terms individually, and we can expect that different Neoclouds may end up with different revenue share and backstop schedules.
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis said Nvidia's GPU backstops typically run for six years, with pre-agreed prices that vary over time and terms negotiated individually with each Neocloud.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: The below table is an illustrative example to explain the basic terms of the program – we present a backstop pricing curve that we believe to be on the lower end of the backstop range – in this case at an average of $2.36 over the six-year period, but we expect that most Neoclouds will negotiate higher backstops.
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis modeled an illustrative six-year Nvidia backstop averaging $2.36 per GPU-hour, which it considered at the low end of the range and below what most Neoclouds would negotiate.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: Over the six years of this scenario, the Nvidia take rate works out to be about 18% on average, but without the backstop, there would be no cluster!
evidence.one_line: In SemiAnalysis's illustrative six-year short-term-rental scenario, Nvidia's average revenue share was about 18%.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: We see that the short-term 1y rental book scenario clearly offers the best IRR among the backstopped scenarios at 25.4%, and these IRRs could realize even higher if the rental market turns out to be strong enough such that 1y and shorter rental rates decay by less than we modeled in the curve below. As expected, the IRRs are higher without a backstop – reaching as high as 40.7% when renting for 1y tenors with no backstop. But if Neoclouds activate the backstop and rent to Nvidia at those prices, they can expect to earn zero or negative IRRs.
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis modeled a 25.4% project IRR for a backstopped one-year rental book, up to 40.7% without a backstop, and zero or negative IRR if the Neocloud had to rent to Nvidia under the backstop.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: When it comes to the Nvidia backstop, banks look at the DSCR ratios assuming revenue earned under the scenario where the backstop is activated. They are looking for a DSCR of at least 1.3x, particularly for the first few years of GPU financing agreement and size their loans to ensure that this bar is met. This typically corresponds to a 70-80% loan to value (LTV) ratio.
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis said lenders assessing Nvidia-backed GPU loans target at least 1.3x DSCR under backstop activation, typically corresponding to 70–80% LTV.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: The first is SharonAI’s 72MW AI factory in Australia. Announced in June 2026, the deal has SharonAI scaling up to as many as 40,000 GB300s under a six-year backstop. Sharon disclosed a total backstop value of $4.88B, which works out to an implied floor of about $2.33/hr/GPU on average over the six year period.
evidence.one_line: SharonAI announced a six-year Nvidia backstop for up to 40,000 GB300 GPUs at its 72MW Australian AI factory, disclosing a $4.88 billion total backstop value and an implied average floor of about $2.33 per GPU-hour.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: Sharon AI’s footprint is now set to grow to 132MW with 102MW contracted, and the company guides to reaching more than 55,000 Nvidia GPUs in total (inclusive of the 40,000 GB300s backstopped) by mid-2027.
evidence.one_line: SharonAI guided to more than 55,000 Nvidia GPUs in total by mid-2027, including the 40,000 backstopped GB300s, and a 132MW footprint with 102MW contracted.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: Firmus’s 360MW AI Cluster in Batam, Indonesia is the next major project announced with an Nvidia backstop. It will likely be housed in a DayOne facility in Kabil Industrial Tech Park (KITP). Announced just recently on June 29 th , 2026, this project shows the scale at which Nvidia is rolling out the backstop program.
evidence.one_line: Firmus announced a 360MW AI cluster in Batam, Indonesia, with an Nvidia backstop, likely to be housed in DayOne's Kabil Industrial Tech Park facility; the project was announced June 29, 2026.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: Firmus announced that they expect $25B to $30B of customer revenue over the six years.
evidence.one_line: Firmus expected $25 billion to $30 billion of customer revenue over six years for its backstopped cluster project.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: Beyond this – Firmus also announced a 600MW firm-energy deal with Gunvor that will also underwrite 1.2GW of new renewables development and 1.5GWh of storage in South Australia by 2032.
evidence.one_line: Firmus announced a 600MW firm-energy deal with Gunvor to support 1.2GW of new renewables development and 1.5GWh of storage in South Australia by 2032.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis

evidence.quote: Nvidia’s backstop program is only getting started, and we see announcements coming faster every quarter. Many Neoclouds are already deep in negotiations with Nvidia, and there are still others that are considering engaging with the backstop program.
evidence.one_line: SemiAnalysis said Nvidia backstop announcements were accelerating and that many Neoclouds were in negotiations, with others considering joining the program.
evidence.speaker: SemiAnalysis
